messages:
zira (cs): FYI AcmeHealth reporting intermittent 429s from their Dedicated reserved pool in us-east-1 during their nightly billing job. They say this started after a spike last Tuesday. Reserved pool id: rp-9182. SLA is 99.9% and they expect smoothing for short bursts. Ticket INC-8342.
maya (support): Thanks — can you paste a sample request/response that shows the 429? Are there X-RateLimit headers or a request_id we can search for in logs?
zira (cs): Customer pasted one example, here it is:
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-large","prompt":"...","max_tokens":1024}'
```
Response snippet they captured:
```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 150
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1765554300
Retry-After: 8
Request-Id: req_64a7b2f9
```
They say this happens in short bursts during a 10–15 minute window each night.
liam (runtime eng): quick summary of expected behavior: Dedicated reserved pools use a per-pool token-bucket + per-route soft-QPS caps. When the token bucket depletes we return 429s with headers like those above. Autoscaler can add nodes but only if the pool is allowed to scale beyond the customer's committed nodes and underlying cloud quota exists. For rp-9182 our config shows steady_qps=150, burst_tokens=500, burst_window=60s.
liam (runtime eng): example pool config (from our control plane):
```json
{"pool_id":"rp-9182","region":"us-east-1","steady_qps":150,"burst_tokens":500,"burst_window_seconds":60}
```
maya (support): Got it. Can SRE check autoscaler events and cloud quota? Also runtime — is there a way to make headers clearer for customers (e.g., include pool id, remaining tokens) so they can correlate?
hugo (sre): checked infra logs for req_64a7b2f9. Autoscaler attempted to add +2 nodes at 2025-11-14T03:12:04Z but the cloud project hit GPU quota for us-east-1 (quota id CLOUD-REQ-123). Scale attempt failed, so effective capacity stayed at committed nodes and token bucket kept draining. Filed cloud quota increase request; support ticket CLOUD-REQ-123.
liam (runtime eng): practical mitigations:
- Short-term: raise pool burst_tokens to 2000 for a limited window (we can do a 6–24h bump) so scheduled jobs can finish.
- Mid-term: increase steady_qps or add a second reserved pool and route high-throughput jobs to it.
- Client-side: recommend exponential backoff + jitter. Our SDKs already implement this; recommend they use SDK retry helper.
liam (runtime eng): sample response we return so they can build backoff logic:
```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 150
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1765554300
Retry-After: 8
X-Redwood-Pool: rp-9182
```
We can add more verbose headers on request (e.g., X-Redwood-Tokens-Remaining) for a short test patch if needed.
maya (support): SRE — can you push the temporary bump (burst_tokens -> 2000) for up to 6 hours while we confirm with the customer? If cloud quota blocks scaling we should communicate that clearly.
hugo (sre): I can apply a temporary bump for 6h. Note: this only helps if the pool hasn't permanently hit committed node limits. If they have a hard reserved node count at commit, boosting burst_tokens helps smooth CPU/GPU scheduling but won't magically add GPUs beyond cloud quota. I'll also escalate CLOUD-REQ-123 with priority.
deploy-bot: autoscaler: scale_event rp-9182 attempted +2 nodes -> failed (cloud quota). event_id ev-20251114-31204
maya (support): Noted. Zira — please confirm with AcmeHealth if they want the 6h bump now. Also ask them to switch their nightly job to the SDK retry helper and add Client-Retry-After logging so we can correlate.
zira (cs): Reached out; they approved a 6h bump to cover tonight's run. I'll attach logs and the exact window to INC-8342. Thanks everyone. I'll loop back after the run.
maya (support): Action items: (1) SRE to apply 6h burst_tokens bump for rp-9182 (hugo), (2) Runtime to prepare quick header-only patch to expose tokens remaining if possible (liam), (3) CS to confirm customer logs and verify 429s stop (zira). Monitoring: we'll watch 429 rate and pool token metrics for 3 runs. :thumbsup:
